bill.title: To establish the Manufacturing Sovereign Wealth Fund, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would create a Manufacturing Sovereign Wealth Fund, a government investment vehicle intended to support domestic manufacturing. The source material provided does not include sufficient detail about the fund's structure, funding mechanism, investment criteria, or operational rules to describe what specific changes it would make to current law or how it would function in practice.

industries.rationale: The bill explicitly establishes a fund dedicated to manufacturing, which would directly affect this sector's access to capital or support.
A sovereign wealth fund would likely involve financial institutions in fund management, investment operations, or capital deployment.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.
Banking & Finance is also the top donor sector for 2 other members from PA. That points to the industry being big in the state, not to anything about this member.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
